findings.body:
**Do not subtract reservations already included in the starts checkpoint.**

In `src/ops/crq/internal/backfillGate.ts:189`, `at >= observedAt` also matches reservations created before the observation in the same timestamp second.

For example, let remaining=3 and checkpoint=1, with one unreflected reservation already included in that checkpoint. After one ordinary start, the starts delta is 1. This line subtracts the old reservation and changes the delta to 0. `admission` then computes effective remaining=2 and admits, instead of computing 1 and preserving the one-slot reserve.

Capture reservation membership with the observation checkpoint. Subtract only reservation starts included in the later starts delta. Changing `>=` to `>` does not distinguish operations within the same second.
findings.title: Do not subtract reservations already included in the starts checkpoint.

findings.body:
**Preserve Unicode separators inside finding strings.**

JSON permits literal U+0085, U+2028 and U+2029 inside strings. NDJSON uses LF or CRLF as record delimiters. These characters must not split a record. ([rfc-editor.org](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc8259/?utm_source=openai))

For a finding whose `comment` contains a literal U+2028, `splitLines` splits the JSON string. `src/ops/crq/internal/localReviewHarvest.ts:58-65` discards both fragments. With a completed, counted classification, Line 77 then constructs a `clean` receipt with no findings. Split on LF and CRLF instead.
findings.title: Preserve Unicode separators inside finding strings.

findings.body:
**Run cleanup even when publication fails after completion.**

When `republish` rejects, `completeLocalReview` propagates the error, so the exit harvester never reaches its cleanup call. The run worktree can then remain after the item has stopped being active. Ensure cleanup still runs on that path, or have the completion path keep the item pending instead of throwing on a publication failure.
findings.title: Run cleanup even when publication fails after completion.

findings.body:
**Validate every job before returning incomplete canonical evidence.**

With two jobs, `currentFixedEvent` can return null for the first job. This return skips the second job's identity and `sourcePr` checks.

The initial job loop does not check `sourcePr`. If the second entry has `sourcePr=92` but its persisted job has `pr=91`, execution can reach `postSourceComment(92, ...)` and record that job as completed.

Continue validating all jobs. Track missing fixed events separately, then return null after the loop if any event is missing.
findings.title: Validate every job before returning incomplete canonical evidence.

findings.body:
**Reject merge commits in the published repair commit list.**

`mergeHeadEvidence` accepts any commit SHA that is an ancestor of the published head. It then reads changed paths with `git diff-tree` without `-m`, `-c`, or `--cc`. Git prints no paths for a merge commit under those options, so a merge in `input.commits` adds no paths. If the anchors name only part of the merge's repairs, the proof never compares the other repaired paths. A later revert of one of those paths is then accepted. Reject merge commits before `diff-tree`, or require the publication to supply the non-merge commits that contain the repairs.
findings.title: Reject merge commits in the published repair commit list.

findings.body:
**Accept merged heads that descend from the published repair head.**

A fix PR can gain a later commit after publication and then merge. In that case `head` (line 124) differs from `published` (line 125). Line 126 then records `not_fixed` with reason `closed-or-head-mismatch`, and line 145 skips the run. Line 171 applies the same exact-equality rule. The source feedback path accepts this state. `publishRepairSourceFeedback` treats the published head and the merged head as separate values and requires only that the published head be an ancestor of the merged head (`mergeHeadEvidence.ts:94-100`). It then checks that the published repair paths remain present.

Removing the equality checks is not sufficient. The replacement must check that the published head is an ancestor of the merged head and must prove that the published repair changes remain at that head. `CurrentRepairEffects` exposes only `readReceipt`, `prInfo`, `targetRef`, `resolveRef`, and `isAncestor`. It does not expose the diff access that `mergeHeadEvidence` uses, so the containment check requires an injected effect.
findings.title: Accept merged heads that descend from the published repair head.
